rapport_notes: Functional and patient with a distracted, multitasking customer, but the call felt scattered rather than warm.

evidence_quotes.agenda: "What are your biggest concerns for this upcoming move and what are the most important things you want answers on this call today."
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised availability, budget, and single-to-two-story move as concerns; rep responded 'Mm-hmm, it's a check. Okay' and pivoted straight to the hourly rate question -- no follow-up on any of the three items raised.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: N/A -- house size (1600 sqft, garage contents needing an inventory walkthrough) triggered a required virtual walkthrough before pricing could be finalized; call ended with a callback arranged for later that evening.

top_strength: Proactively solved a scheduling conflict by offering an alternate branch (North Austin) to meet the customer's required Saturday date after South Austin was full.
coaching_note: Don't let customer-raised concerns (budget, story-count change) pass with just an acknowledgment -- a single follow-up question would have been enough to hit two-layers-deep credit.
